landing.faq.description: What you need to know about creating, daily check-ins, referrals and using credits.
landing.faq.quality.question: What can I create on this website?
landing.faq.quality.answer: Enter a prompt on the homepage, choose an aspect ratio, then generate with AI Image. Use the dedicated editor for reference-image changes, and the prompt library for posters, products, typography, infographics and UI concepts.
landing.faq.credits.question: How are credits calculated, and are failed tasks refunded?
landing.faq.credits.answer: Default FLUX.2 generation uses 8 credits per image; editing uses 10 credits. Other models show their own quote before submission.
landing.faq.commercial.question: Can I use generated images commercially?
landing.faq.commercial.answer: Commercial use depends on the selected model, provider terms, your prompt, uploaded materials and the rights of people, brands or characters depicted. Review the current Terms and the relevant provider license before publishing; this website cannot grant rights owned by a provider or third party.
landing.faq.models.question: Which AI models and tools are actually available now?
landing.faq.models.answer: Choose from integrated Nano Banana, GPT Image, Seedream and FLUX models. Each model page shows availability and its credit quote.
landing.faq.release_status.question: Can I generate with Wan 3.0 or Seedance 2.5 here today?
landing.faq.release_status.answer: Alibaba Cloud's Wan 3.0 Preview API is live as wan3.0-video in Beijing, but this site's Wan 3.0 generator is not enabled until a real request and billing flow pass end-to-end testing. Seedance 2.5 remains a prompt builder while paid Seedance generation uses the verified 2.0 endpoint.
landing.faq.account.question: Can I try the workflow before signing in?
landing.faq.account.answer: Yes. You can write a prompt and choose the model and aspect ratio first, then sign in when you generate. Your draft is restored after you return. Examples, guides and prompt-planning tools are also available without signing in. The current new-account reward is shown on the sign-in and sign-up pages.
landing.faq.rewards.question: How do daily check-ins and referral rewards work?
landing.faq.rewards.answer: Signed-in users can check in once per day. A seven-day streak awards 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6 and 6 credits, for 33 credits in total; a missed day restarts the streak. Referral links apply to accounts created within the last seven days, and a successful referral gives 10 credits to each person. Duplicate, self-referral and abusive claims are not rewarded.
landing.faq.privacy.question: Are my prompts, uploads and results public?
landing.faq.privacy.answer: They are not displayed publicly by default. Prompts, uploads and results are associated with your account and sent to the configured AI provider when needed to complete a task. Task records may be retained for history, downloads, support and security. Avoid sensitive information and review the Privacy Policy for the full data-handling details.

tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_1_body: A strong YouTube thumbnail does not summarize the entire video. It makes one honest promise that the title and opening seconds can fulfill. Use a concrete subject and a visible consequence; avoid vague decoration that creates attention without setting an expectation.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_1_bullet: Name the object, person, place or transformation viewers should notice first.
Keep the thumbnail idea consistent with the video title rather than repeating every word.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_2_body: Most impressions are judged at a small size and in a crowded feed. Large shapes, separated values and a short title survive reduction. Fine props, several faces and long sentences usually collapse into visual noise even when the full-resolution image looks impressive.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_2_bullet: Zoom the result down until it is roughly the width of a mobile search card.
Reject any result whose focal subject or title needs more than a glance to decode.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_3_body: A curiosity gap works when the image shows an unusual state and the video explains it. Fabricated outcomes, fake metrics and unrelated celebrity faces may increase short-term clicks but damage audience trust and can create policy or rights problems.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_3_bullet: Show the real question, conflict or before-and-after explored in the video.
Do not invent products, quotes, reactions, awards or results that are absent from the content.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_4_body: Generate one coherent direction, then compare only meaningful alternatives: a tighter crop, a different color temperature or a shorter phrase. Save the video topic, thumbnail version, impressions and click-through rate together so future decisions are based on audience evidence rather than personal taste.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.section_4_bullet: Change one major variable between variants so the comparison teaches you something.
Judge click-through rate beside watch time; a click that immediately leaves is not a useful win.
tools.youtube_thumbnail.faq_1_question: Does this AI YouTube thumbnail generator output 16:9 images?

tools.youtube_thumbnail.faq_3_question: Can I copy another creator's thumbnail style?

tools.youtube_thumbnail.faq_4_question: How many words should a thumbnail use?
tools.youtube_thumbnail.faq_4_answer: There is no universal number, but fewer words usually read better at small size. Use the shortest phrase that adds a visual promise not already obvious from the video title.

tools.video.tool_description: The workspace focuses on the variables that determine whether a short clip feels intentional: what changes, how the camera witnesses it, how quickly the action develops and where the final beat lands.
tools.video.example_caption: Three beats · one subject · one visual arc
tools.video.section_1_body: A video prompt needs verbs and sequence. State the opening condition, the physical change and the final state. Describing only a beautiful subject leaves the model to invent motion, which often produces drifting cameras, unstable geometry or an action that never resolves.
tools.video.section_1_bullet_1: Use a beginning, development and final beat that can fit inside five or eight seconds.
tools.video.section_1_bullet_2: Describe observable movement such as unfolding, turning, rising or crossing the frame.
tools.video.section_2_title: Give the camera one clear job
tools.video.section_2_body: Camera instructions should support the action instead of competing with it. A locked frame reveals transformation; a slow push increases attention; a lateral track follows travel. Stacking orbit, zoom, crane and handheld language in one short clip usually reduces continuity.
tools.video.section_2_bullet_1: Choose one dominant move and a stable subject relationship.
tools.video.section_2_bullet_2: Use a locked or gentle camera when subject accuracy matters more than spectacle.
tools.video.section_3_body: Five seconds suits one reveal, gesture or product moment. Eight seconds gives a two-stage transformation room to breathe. Longer is not automatically better: every additional beat increases cost and creates more opportunities for identity drift or unwanted objects.
tools.video.section_3_bullet_1: Use five seconds for a single shot with one decisive action.
tools.video.section_3_bullet_2: Use eight seconds only when the prompt contains a readable second beat.
tools.video.section_4_body: Watch once for the story, then scrub through the clip for shape changes, duplicate objects, flicker, unsafe details and abrupt camera jumps. Generated video is a production asset only after the subject, claims, likeness rights, audio and final destination have been checked.
tools.video.section_4_bullet_1: Compare the first, middle and final frames for identity and geometry.
tools.video.section_4_bullet_2: Keep the accepted prompt, format and duration beside the approved export.

tools.video.faq_2_question: Which formats and durations are available?
tools.video.faq_2_answer: The page offers 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 formats with controlled 5 or 8 second durations at 720p. These choices cover common landscape, vertical and square placements while keeping costs predictable.
tools.video.faq_3_question: Why does video generation take longer than image generation?
tools.video.faq_3_answer: The model must create many temporally consistent frames rather than one image. Queue load and duration affect render time, so the task remains asynchronous and can take several minutes.
tools.video.faq_4_question: What happens if the provider task fails?
tools.video.faq_4_answer: A failed task is marked as failed and its consumed credits are restored by the existing transactional task system. Temporary status errors remain retryable before the final timeout.
tools.video.faq_5_question: Can I generate videos with real people or copyrighted characters?
tools.video.faq_5_answer: Only use people, characters, music and source material you have the right to use. Do not create deceptive impersonation, non-consensual intimate material or misleading evidence, and review provider and destination-platform policies.

tools.background_remover.section_1_title: Give the model a separable subject
tools.background_remover.section_1_body: Background removal is most reliable when the subject has a readable silhouette and enough contrast from its surroundings. Overlapping objects, severe motion blur and a subject cropped by the frame create uncertain boundaries that no interface can fully recover.
tools.background_remover.section_1_bulle: Use the highest-resolution original available instead of a compressed screenshot.
Keep the complete product, person or object inside the frame when possible.
tools.background_remover.section_2_body: Hair, fur, feathers, translucent fabric, glass, smoke and reflections contain partial transparency. Zoom in against both light and dark backgrounds; an edge that looks correct on a checkerboard may reveal halos after placement on a saturated campaign color.
tools.background_remover.section_2_bulle: Check thin structures such as straps, handles, spokes and fingers separately.
Look for color spill from the old background around reflective or pale edges.
tools.background_remover.section_3_title: Use transparency as a production layer
tools.background_remover.section_3_body: A clean cutout is not automatically a finished product image. Add a destination-appropriate canvas, realistic contact shadow and consistent scale. Marketplace main images, advertisements and editorial composites each have different accuracy and disclosure requirements.
tools.background_remover.section_3_bulle: Keep an untouched original beside every approved transparent export.
Do not add a new context that falsely changes the product's size, contents or use.
tools.background_remover.section_4_title: Review the result with a moving boundary
tools.background_remover.section_4_body: A fixed side-by-side pair makes small geometry changes difficult to notice. The sweeping divider places original and result on the same coordinates, so missing corners, softened edges and leftover background become visible exactly where the boundary crosses.
tools.background_remover.section_4_bulle: Pause the divider over high-detail areas and compare the same pixels.
Test the exported PNG on at least one light and one dark final background.
tools.background_remover.faq_1_question: Does the tool return a transparent PNG?
tools.background_remover.faq_1_answer: Yes. The processing service returns a PNG with an alpha channel, and the result is presented over a checkerboard so transparency can be inspected before download.
tools.background_remover.faq_2_answer: High-resolution images with one clear foreground subject, visible boundaries and moderate background contrast work best. Tiny subjects, motion blur, fog and overlapping transparent objects are harder.
tools.background_remover.faq_3_answer: The tool requires sign-in and uses the site's configured storage path so the provider can retrieve the source. Do not upload confidential or restricted material, and review the site's privacy policy and provider terms.
tools.background_remover.faq_4_question: Why should I inspect the cutout on different colors?
tools.background_remover.faq_4_answer: White halos, dark fringes and old-background color spill can hide on one background and become obvious on another. Testing both light and dark surfaces is a fast edge-quality check.
tools.background_remover.faq_5_question: What happens when background removal fails?
tools.background_remover.faq_5_answer: Provider failures enter the same final task state and credit restoration flow used by the other paid AI tools. You can then retry with a cleaner or higher-resolution source.

nano_site.home.title: Nano Banana 2.1 AI Image Generator & Editor

nano_site.home.intro: Turn an idea into an image. Write a prompt, bring your references, and choose the Nano Banana model that fits. Keep faces, products and the words in your picture in focus.
nano_site.home.section_0.title: What is Nano Banana 2.1?
nano_site.home.section_0.body:
Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's image generation and editing model, identified as gemini-nano-banana-2.1. Released on October 6, 2026, it updates Nano Banana 2. Use it to describe a new scene or plan changes to an existing image; the selected model and available controls determine the actual request.

Begin with the image's purpose. A catalog photo needs recognizable product details and space for copy. A poster needs an ordered layout and verified wording. This independent workspace helps you prepare those decisions before spending credits.
nano_site.home.section_1.title: Nano Banana 2.1 vs Nano Banana 2
nano_site.home.section_1.body:
An upgrade deserves a test with your own work. Keep a successful Nano Banana 2 brief, its reference files and the finished image. Prepare the same task for 2.1 and compare the features that matter: lettering, subject identity, layout and preserved details.

Keep both model names in your records. If a parameter is unavailable on one model, note the difference rather than hiding it in the comparison. The migration guide explains how to build a small acceptance set before changing an established workflow.
nano_site.home.section_2.title: Nano Banana 2.1 vs Pro: choose for the task
nano_site.home.section_2.body:
Pro and 2.1 are separate model choices. Define success before comparing them: a readable poster headline, a product that keeps its proportions, or a character whose identifying features survive an edit. A striking sample alone cannot answer all three questions.

Use the same prompt and references, then inspect the outputs at the size where people will use them. Include the quote and the number of corrections in your decision. Our Pro comparison guide provides a review method; we have not published a measured winner or a guaranteed speed advantage.
nano_site.home.section_3.title: Plan references, text and output shape
nano_site.home.section_3.body:
Give each reference a role: the first supplies product geometry, another supplies a color direction, and a layout sketch establishes placement. State which details must remain, such as a face shape, bottle silhouette or camera angle. Extra images help only when their purpose is clear.

Write important text exactly and specify its position. Choose a shape for the destination before requesting more detail: a square catalog card, portrait poster or wide banner. Available resolutions and reference limits can vary by model and service, so use the controls actually offered in the workbench.
nano_site.home.section_4.title: How to use the workbench
nano_site.home.section_4.body:
Choose a task, write a brief and select the output shape. For an edit, add a reference and separate the requested change from the preservation list. You can copy the prompt or download the brief without an account.

Sign in to generate. Nano Banana 2.1 uses 8 credits for one 1K image or reference edit. Review the quote, submit once, then follow the task status and download the finished result.

nano_site.home.faq_2.question: Is Pro the same model as 2.1?
nano_site.home.faq_2.answer: No. They are separate model choices. Compare the same task, references, supported settings and actual quote before selecting one.
nano_site.home.faq_3.question: How do I write a prompt with readable text?
nano_site.home.faq_3.answer: Provide the exact wording in quotation marks, specify its location and keep the number of text blocks small. Inspect every letter at the final size; use editable manual text for critical labels.
nano_site.prompts.title: Nano Banana 2.1 Prompts: Products, Posters & Reference Edits
nano_site.prompts.description: Adapt original Nano Banana 2.1 prompts for product photos, readable posters, reference edits and scientific schematics. Copy a brief and review it step by step.
nano_site.prompts.heading: Nano Banana 2.1 prompts you can adapt
nano_site.prompts.intro: Start with the task you want to finish. Each recipe gives you a subject, composition and constraints to replace with your own details; the workbench lets you copy or save the brief.
nano_site.prompts.section_0.title: Build a prompt from five concrete decisions
nano_site.prompts.section_0.body:
Write the subject and its action, the composition, the lighting or material, any exact text, and the constraints. For example: one cobalt bottle, centered on pale stone, light from the left, no lettering, empty space above. Each part describes something you can inspect in the result.

Keep the first attempt focused. A wide-angle documentary photograph and a flat vector icon ask for different visual rules. Choose one direction, then describe the detail that makes it yours. Add words when they remove ambiguity, such as where a shadow falls or which object sits in front.
nano_site.prompts.section_1.title: Write product and character edits as change-and-preserve briefs
nano_site.prompts.section_1.body:
For a product edit, say: replace the background with a neutral studio wall; preserve the silhouette, label position, cap, reflections and crop. For a character, preserve face shape, hairstyle, clothing colors and distinguishing accessories while changing the pose or location.

Give each uploaded reference an explicit role. A subject photo provides identity; a style image provides color or lighting. If a result changes a required detail, make the next brief about that specific error. Repeating 'keep everything the same' is less useful than naming the features you will check.
nano_site.prompts.section_2.title: Create a poster with a readable text hierarchy
nano_site.prompts.section_2.body:
Put the headline and date in quotation marks and specify how many text blocks belong in the image. A useful starting brief might ask for one large headline near the top, a short date below and an uncluttered illustration in the lower half. Reserve space for a venue or fine print that you can typeset later.

Inspect spelling, punctuation and reading order at the final export size. Check for invented sponsors, duplicate letters and unwanted text in the background. For product ingredients, legal disclosures or a final logo, add verified lettering in a manual layer so it remains editable.
nano_site.prompts.section_3.title: Prompt a scientific schematic without inventing evidence
nano_site.prompts.section_3.body:
State the figure's role first: a conceptual workflow for explanation. Define the panels, exact labels and allowed arrows before describing the palette. The scientific recipe below uses sample preparation, measurement, analysis and review with no numerical values or experimental imagery.

Replace generic stages with terminology checked by a subject expert. If you need a chart, plot your actual dataset separately and combine it with an approved schematic in a layout tool. Keep the caption explicit about which parts are conceptual; the scientific figures guide includes a label-review checklist.
nano_site.prompts.faq_0.question: Do these prompts guarantee the same image?
nano_site.prompts.faq_0.answer: No. The model, references, settings and generation variability affect each result. A recipe supplies an inspectable brief; keep a baseline and change one requirement at a time.
nano_site.prompts.faq_1.question: Can I copy a prompt directly into the workbench?
nano_site.prompts.faq_1.answer: Yes. Load a recipe, replace the subject, check the model and credit quote, and generate. You can also copy or download the brief for free.
nano_site.comparison.title: Nano Banana 2.1 vs Pro: Compare the Same Image Brief
nano_site.comparison.description: Compare Nano Banana 2.1 and Pro with the same prompts and references. Review text, identity, edits and actual cost without unsupported quality rankings.
nano_site.comparison.heading: Nano Banana 2.1 vs Pro: which fits your image?
nano_site.comparison.intro: Choose around a task you can check. This guide separates model identity and available options from results that still need a real comparison.
nano_site.comparison.section_0.title: Start with the decision you need to make
nano_site.comparison.section_0.body:
Nano Banana 2.1 and Nano Banana Pro are separate image-model choices. Their official positioning helps narrow a shortlist, but it does not establish which one will meet a particular poster, product edit or character brief. Write down the required output before choosing.

A poster might pass only when the headline is correct and the hierarchy is clear. A product image might pass only when its silhouette, label and crop are preserved. Treat these as separate criteria; a pleasant color palette cannot compensate for a wrong product shape.
nano_site.comparison.section_1.title: Use the same prompt and references
nano_site.comparison.section_1.body:
Prepare one new-image brief and one reference-edit brief. Keep the wording, reference files and requested layout identical, and use the closest matching output shape and size. Record any settings that one model does not offer so the comparison can be understood later.

Keep the unedited output from each attempt. If you repair a title manually or crop an image, record that work separately. When budget allows, use more than one attempt for each task and show all attempts; selecting only a favorite conceals the revision effort.
nano_site.comparison.section_2.title: Review text, identity and composition separately
nano_site.comparison.section_2.body:
Read every requested word at the final viewing size. Check whether the result adds extra captions or changes punctuation. For references, compare distinctive facial features, product proportions, logos and camera angle with the original. For new scenes, inspect element placement and unwanted objects.

Use a simple record: pass, needs correction or unusable, followed by a specific reason. 'The bottle cap became wider' is useful; 'looks less professional' is difficult to act on. Decide which failures are acceptable before seeing the results so style preferences do not replace the original brief.
nano_site.comparison.section_3.title: Include cost and revision effort
nano_site.comparison.section_3.body:
Record the displayed credit quote and the number of revisions needed for a useful result. Nano Banana 2.1 uses 8 credits per 1K generation or reference edit; Pro uses 15 credits.

Both models can be selected in the workbench. Compare them with your own prompts and references. These credit quotes are website billing rules, not official Google prices or measured speed benchmarks.
nano_site.comparison.faq_0.question: Is Nano Banana 2.1 always better than Pro?
nano_site.comparison.faq_0.answer: This page does not establish an overall winner. Test the same important task on both named models and compare failures, available settings, total cost and revision effort.
